title: Yeşil Dönüşüm Metalleri, Küresel Risk ve Makroekonomik Belirsizliklerin BIST Sürdürülebilirlik Endeksi Üzerindeki Etkileri: ARDL Yaklaşımı
journal: Bulletin of Economic Theory and Analysis
abstract: Bu çalışma, BIST Sürdürülebilirlik Endeksi (XUSRD) ile küresel risk algısı, ABD 10 yıllık tahvil faizleri, Brent Petrol, Türkiye’nin ekonomik politika belirsizliği, döviz kuru ve yeşil enerji geçişinin temel girdileri olan nikel ve bakır fiyatları arasındaki ilişkileri, 2015:01–2024:12 dönemi için ARDL eşbütünleşme ve Toda-Yamamoto nedensellik yöntemleri çerçevesinde incelemektedir. Elde edilen bulgular, XUSRD’nin küresel makro-finansal şoklar ile Türkiye’ye özgü ekonomik dinamikler ara-sında dengeli fakat hassas bir yapı sergilediğini göstermektedir. Endeks üzerinde VIX ve petrol fiyat-larının baskılayıcı bir etkisi bulunurken; döviz kuru ile ABD 10 yıllık tahvil faizlerinin endeksi pozitif yönde etkilediği görülmüştür. Enerji geçiş metallerinden, nikel fiyatlarının kısa dönemde endeks üze-rinde anlamlı ve pozitif bir etki yarattığı, uzun dönemde ise hem nikel hem de bakır fiyatlarının etkisi-nin istatistiksel olarak ortadan kalktığı bulgulanmıştır. Toda-Yamamoto nedensellik testi ile destekle-nen bulgular, XUSRD’nin küresel belirsizlik ve emtia kaynaklı şoklara karşı doğrusal bir kırılganlık yerine, belirgin bir yapısal direnç sergilediğini ortaya koymaktadır. Ampirik bulgular, sürdürülebilir yatırımların makro-finansal şoklara karşı duyarlılığını ortaya koyarken; çalışma, küresel risk, yerel belirsizlik ve stratejik emtiaları bütüncül bir modelde birleştirmesi bakımından özgün bir nitelik taşı-maktadır. Elde edilen sonuçlar, sürdürülebilir portföylerin yönetiminde geleneksel göstergelerin yanı sıra stratejik emtia fiyatlarının da takip edilmesinin kritik önemine işaret etmektedir.

title: Where learning meets knowledge: Human resource development professionals as catalysts for advancing the human resource development–knowledge management agenda in South Africa
journal: SA Journal of Human Resource Management
abstract: Orientation: There is renewed interest in knowledge management (KM) due to the current global emphasis on technology. Knowledge management is crucial for developing the required competence, thereby placing it within the human resource development (HRD) domain. Research purpose: This research explored the extent to which, if any, human resource development practitioners (HRDPs) in South Africa apply KM activities in practice. Motivation for the study: Although HRD utilises KM activities such as knowledge sharing and prominent writers highlight the importance of KM within HRD, little is known about whether and how other KM activities, namely knowledge transfer, acquisition, creation, application, capture and storage, are applied in practice within an HRD context. Hence, this study sought to gather the perspectives of HRDPs in South Africa on the application of KM. Research approach/design and method: The study employed a qualitative, interpretive research design. Twelve HRDPs selected through expert sampling were individually interviewed to collect data. Data were analysed manually using content analysis. Main findings: Human resource development practitioners apply all KM activities, although they did not identify all activities by name in every instance. Practical/managerial implications: The study informs HRD practice on how KM is applied in an HRD context with specific HRD examples related to KM activities. Contribution/value-add: This empirical study is one of the limited few that explores the application of KM within an HRD context and from HRDPs’ perspectives.

title: When the past looks safer: nostalgia, logo stability and brand trust judgements
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
abstract: This study advances branding theory by complementing and refining dominant affect-centric accounts of nostalgia by introducing a parallel cognitive pathway. It examines whether nostalgic logo design enhances brand trust through stability-based cognitive inference rather than emotional nostalgia, addressing an unresolved puzzle concerning why past-oriented visual cues generate future-oriented judgements of reliability under uncertainty. Four-experiment research programme tests the proposed mechanism. Across controlled and ecologically realistic settings, it establishes the focal effect of nostalgic logo design on brand trust, identifies perceived visual stability as the mediating mechanism, specifies uncertainty avoidance as a theoretically grounded boundary condition and provides evidence consistent with a causal mechanism using a real-world brand interface. Rival explanations, including familiarity, processing fluency, brand attitude and affective nostalgia, are systematically ruled out. Nostalgic logo design increases brand trust by enhancing perceived visual stability, which functions as a cognitive safety signal that reduces perceived uncertainty. This stability-based pathway operates selectively among consumers high in uncertainty avoidance and remains robust in low-narrative, low-affect logo contexts. Moderated mediation analyses confirm that nostalgic logo design acts as a contingent trust signal rather than a universal evaluative enhancer. The study reconceptualises nostalgia for branding as an inferential resource rather than an affective response. By introducing perceived visual stability as a novel mechanism linking visual identity to trust formation and identifying uncertainty avoidance as a mechanistic boundary condition, the research integrates visual identity into trust theory and provides actionable guidance for logo redesign decisions under conditions of heightened uncertainty.

title: Warehouse logistics and task switching theory revisited: asymmetric height switching costs in order picking systems
journal: International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the impact of pick location height switching on task performance time in manual order picking systems. Drawing on task switching theory, we examine whether switching between ground- and chest-level pick locations increases task performance time, whether switching costs are asymmetric, and whether item weight strengthens possible differences between ground-to-chest and chest-to-ground switches. Design/methodology/approach We adopt a two-stage approach that combines internal validity and operational generalizability. First, a controlled eye-tracking experiment simulates a simplified order picking scenario to explore the cognitive mechanisms underlying visual search when repeating versus switching pick location heights. Second, we analyze 3,537,973 pick location visits from a German grocery retail warehouse to test the effects of pick location height switching in a real-world operational environment with professional order pickers. Findings The eye-tracking experiment provides mechanism-oriented evidence that switching between pick location heights increases visual search time and reorientation demands under controlled conditions. The archival field study complements these behavioral insights by showing that height switching is associated with longer task performance time. It further shows that switching costs depend on direction, with ground-to-chest switches being more time-consuming than chest-to ground switches. This directional difference becomes more pronounced as item weight increases. Practical implications The findings suggest that warehouse managers should consider not only the frequency but also the direction of height switches when designing picking sequences. Batching and routing algorithms could incorporate switching costs as a weighted parameter, with particular attention to ground-to-chest switches involving heavier items. However, reducing height switches should be balanced against ergonomic risks, as long sequences of ground-level picks may increase repetitive bending and musculoskeletal strain. Originality/value This study provides the first empirical evidence on pick location height switching in warehouse operations and extends task switching theory to a new operational context. By combining mechanism-oriented eye-tracking evidence with large-scale field data, we show that height switching is associated with asymmetric switching costs and provide insights into the cognitive and motor reorientation processes that may underlie these effects.

title: The response of multinational and international organisations to resilience and sustainability in Latin America and the Caribbean: future directions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the theoretical foundations of resilience and sustainability in relation to multinational enterprises and international organisations operating in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). It provides an understanding of how resilience and sustainability can be developed in the context of multinational enterprises and international organisations in LAC. Design/methodology/approach Using the PRISMA methodology, 61 academic articles were analysed using a mixed-methods approach that combined quantitative and qualitative techniques. The study identifies and analyses the Sustainable Development Goals addressed in the literature. Findings The study provides a structured synthesis of how multinational enterprises and international organisations address resilience and sustainability in LAC, highlighting gaps in contextual analysis and database coverage. It identifies the principal research themes and reveals four thematic clusters. The findings emphasise the need to broaden the scope of future research and highlight implications for policy and practice. Opportunities for cross-sector collaboration among academia, businesses, policymakers and international organisations are also discussed. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, this study is among the first to provide a comprehensive synthesis of research on resilience and sustainability in relation to multinational enterprises and international organisations in LAC. By integrating bibliometric and content analyses, it maps the intellectual structure of the field, identifies key research themes and knowledge gaps and develops a future research agenda. The findings offer valuable insights for scholars, practitioners and policymakers seeking to strengthen resilience and sustainability strategies within the international business context of LAC.

title: The final count-down: estimating the total value of all the world's natural resources and an estimate of how long they may last
abstract: Introduction We have attempted a final count-down of all resources available to human society in future and converted this to monetary value for 2026. Methods Simulations using the WORLD7 Integrated Assessment Model explore how long the available resources will support wealth and value creation in the global society. Results The estimates made suggests that about 75% of the world's value creation has its origin in natural resources, and about 2 / 3 of the value creation has its origin in finite, fossil natural resources, fossil energy, fossil metals, and fossil materials. Our results suggests that a system reconfiguration, including thorium-based technologies, would be required for making society last more than 1,000 generations. The most valuable resources in analysis are the energy resources, but these are partly dependent on the availability of technology metals and materials. Thorium appears to be the single most valuable energy resource on the list, provided thorium-based power plants are adopted, and based on the energy price. The gross revenue from resource extraction and the profit value of the annual production was estimated. The recoverable resource stocks of natural resources and the annual extraction rates were estimated. Discussion Our estimates were combined with earlier estimates of the value of the ecosystems on the Earth and estimates of the value of the geo- and biosphere to society. The model simulations point to the importance of a long-term material circularity, minimizing losses of material and preserving resource quality with time. The simulation outputs suggest the material resources will last about 250–400 years from the global industrialization in 1900 to about 2350. It appears that adjusting the settings of the present system is not sufficient for a fully sustainable society. The final conclusion is that natural resources are root currency of the human civilization, equivalent to what we call money, concurrent with Odums 1996 seminal book.

title: Targeting Alzheimer’s disease pathways with Caralluma dalzielii: behavioural, biochemical, and molecular evidence from a transgenic Drosophila melanogaster model
Servant leadership effects on service climate and employee engagement: a multi-level analysis
abstract: Purpose This study examined the multi-level relationships between servant leadership, service climate, and employee engagement. It investigated how store manager servant leadership cultivated group trust at the store level, consequently affecting service climate and influenced employee engagement through perceived supervisor support. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a multi-level design to investigate the relationships. Data were collected in two waves from a total of 1,409 restaurant employees in Thailand, with usable responses obtained from 801 individuals across 120 restaurants who completed both waves of the survey in full. On average, teams had 6.68 members. A multi-level structural equation modeling approach was employed to account for the nested structure of employees within restaurant, enabling simultaneous testing of individual-level and store-level relationships. Findings Store manager servant leadership indirectly influenced employee engagement through perceived supervisor support. Additionally, servant leadership cultivated group trust at the store level, which, in turn, positively impacted service climate. Practical implications Organizations can significantly improve employee engagement by fostering leaders who value empathy, humility, and the well-being of their teams. Additionally, by prioritizing employee growth and creating a supportive environment built on trust, organizations can also build a positive work climate. Originality/value This study enhances our understanding of servant leadership by demonstrating its indirect influence on employee engagement. The multi-level approach provides a more refined view of how this leadership style shapes organizational dynamics. Specifically, it highlights the importance of servant leadership in building trust and fostering service climate.
